answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to periodically complete a unique, non-parallelizable computation bound to its own key - a thread of work no other identity can reuse. Running one identity is cheap, but an attacker spawning thousands faces a cost that scales linearly with every fake, like an echo that multiplies with each copy. Honest agents pass the check at dawn of each cycle and keep trading; fakes that cannot afford the work simply starve out of the market.
